$comment: AUTHORITATIVE, NORMATIVE derivation-table source for the Distractor Derivation Model (DDM). This JSON — together with tests/fixtures/unit_tables.json — is the SOLE normative authority for shared derivation configuration. Runtime files (agent-go/derivation_tables_gen.go, src/derivation_tables_gen.ts, functions/src/ai/derivation_tables_gen.ts, and the Dart subset) are GENERATED from these bytes by scripts/gen_derivation_tables.mjs and must never be hand-edited. Inline design tables and worked examples in design.md are explanatory and non-normative; on any conflict, THIS JSON WINS. All shared numbers are stored as exact integer or fixed-point encodings (multiplicative factors in permille = factor*1000; additive deltas and offsets as integer/decimal magnitudes with an explicit scale) — never binary floating literals. Values seeded from agent-go/guardrails.go (DeriveOffsetsFromSurprise, canonicalizeSurpriseFactor, yearDelta) but this JSON, not those literals, is authoritative.

closed_sets.$comment: All closed enumerations referenced elsewhere in this file. The generator rejects any reference to a value not listed here.

canonical_surprise.$comment: Canonicalization of surprise_factor to the 0-3 band. Canonical keys 0-3 map to themselves. Legacy keys 4-10 use the exact source mapping from canonicalizeSurpriseFactor (4:1, 5:2, 6:2, 7:2, 8:3, 9:3, 10:3). Negative inputs clamp to 0. Missing/invalid schema values use `schema_default`. Values strictly above `legacy_max` follow `upper_clamp`.

base_distance_bands.$comment: Four ordered base multiplicative bands selected by canonical surprise. Stored in permille (factor * 1000) as exact integers, never binary floats. Semantics: candidate above truth = true * factor; candidate below truth = true / factor. Row 3 carries a magnitude-dependent max via magnitude_calibration (small = 5.000x, large = 4.000x); its `factor_max_permille` here is the small-magnitude value and the large variant is applied by magnitude_calibration. Ordering is enforced: for every adjacent pair (s, s+1) both min and max at s+1 are >= those at s. Seeded from DeriveOffsetsFromSurprise.

kind_strategies.$comment: Arithmetic family selected per resolved quantity_kind. `year` is additive and calendar-bounded; `percentage` and `rating` are bounded additive within a fixed scale; other kinds are multiplicative by default. `zero_uses_zero_value_strategy` marks kinds whose zero truth routes to zero_value_strategy instead of multiplicative arithmetic (every non-year kind).

kind_band_conversions.$comment: For additive/bounded kinds, four ordered raw delta intervals derived from the same surprise semantics. Deltas are exact integers/decimals with an explicit scale. Each kind lists one interval per canonical surprise (index 0..3). Ordering is enforced: both delta_min and delta_max are non-decreasing across surprise. `year` deltas are seeded from yearDelta (5, 12, 40, 100) as fixed additive year offsets. Multiplicative kinds have no conversion here; they use base_distance_bands directly.

magnitude_calibration.$comment: Selects the small/large variant of the chosen surprise ROW and picks the snap quantum; it never redirects to a different surprise row. `small_max_exclusive` = 10 mirrors the source `trueNumber < 10` split. For band 3 the large variant caps the max factor at 4.000x (large_factor_max_permille), matching DeriveOffsetsFromSurprise. calibration_ids are stable generated identifiers used in observability.

bounds_defaults.$comment: Deterministic kind-derived plausibility bounds used only when no valid Fact Bank or model bounds_hint survives. `mult_lo_permille`/`mult_hi_permille` derive bounds multiplicatively from |true| for unbounded kinds; `zero_default_max` provides the default upper bound when true_number == 0 so zero-value additive distractors fit within plausibility bounds; fixed_min/fixed_max apply for kinds with a fixed scale (with optional mult_lo_permille/mult_hi_permille fallback when true_number exceeds fixed_max, e.g. rating > 10). A resolved pair must satisfy plausible_min <= true_number <= plausible_max; otherwise the model abstains with BOUNDS_INCOHERENT. `year.retrospective_ceiling` fixes the normative upper bound for retrospective past milestones (true_number <= retrospective_ceiling) so past events never generate absurd future-year decoys; it is updated at generation time by scripts/gen_derivation_tables.mjs. Future-dated events (true_number > retrospective_ceiling) remain unclamped.

unit_bounds_overrides.$comment: Hard domain ceilings/floors keyed by NORMALIZED unit (post-normalization spelling: lowercase, single spaces). After bounds resolve (Fact-Bank hint, model hint, or kind default), the resolved pair is intersected with the unit's override pair and re-checked for coherence: a physical/rule ceiling constrains even hint-provided bounds, and a true_number outside the override yields BOUNDS_INCOHERENT. Seed ONLY mathematically or rule-true limits (e.g. the NFL passer-rating formula caps at 158.3); soft priors belong in per-fact plausible_min/plausible_max hints, never here. Bound tokens are canonical numeric strings ingested by exact Numeric_Ingest, never floats.

hard_boundaries.$comment: Quantity-kind domain limits that a candidate must satisfy independently of plausibility bounds. A candidate on the invalid side is rejected, never clamped. `min_inclusive`/`max_inclusive` are exact; null means no boundary on that end. integer_only forces integral candidates (count). Seeded from Giveaway Gate rules 5.8 (count >= 0) and 5.9 (percentage <= 100).

dead_zones.$comment: The band immediately around true_number inside which a candidate is too obvious and must be rejected. `half_width_permille` is a fraction of |true| (permille of the true magnitude); `min_absolute` with `min_absolute_scale` guarantees a floor for tiny/zero truths. A candidate c is inside the dead zone when |c - true| < max(|true| * half_width_permille/1000, min_absolute). Applies per kind. Percentage uses an absolute floor only (1.0 point): a 5% multiplicative dead zone around 95 swallows the surprise-0 additive band of 1.5-3.0 points, collapsing every surprise onto the same snapped 90.

candidate_order.$comment: Deterministic variation-slot enumeration and the finite remedy ladder. `slot_count` fixes how many evenly spaced slots span each band interval; slot0 is chosen by FNV-1a over the variation key and remaining slots are walked in the fixed order below. `variation_key_fields` is the exact, ordered set of canonical DDM determinants used to build the key — it deliberately excludes candidate_side, round_number, topic, clocks, and pack/round difficulty metadata. `remedy_stages` is the finite, ordered remedy sequence (first-pass-wins). All non-crossing stages exhaust on the required side before any crossing stage runs: `opposite_side` retries the calibrated band on the other side, and `opposite_bound_derived` is the last-resort bound interpolation on that same other side (reachable only when the opposite band itself cannot land a candidate, e.g. a small-count band collapsing onto landmark values).

snapping.$comment: Significant-figure / natural-number snapping. The initial step is selected by (quantity_kind, magnitude_scale); the refinement sequence is evaluated in index order and the first invariant-preserving snapped value wins. `two_sig_fig` leads so the deterministic 8-slot band variation survives snapping (e.g. slots around a 4000-truth stay 4600/4700/.../5400 instead of all collapsing to one_sig_fig's 5000); `one_sig_fig` is the first fallback when a two-figure snap violates an invariant, and half_step/unit_step terminate the ladder. Steps are exact powers-of-ten quanta expressed as (step_mantissa * 10^step_exp). Midpoint magnitudes round away from zero. Count outputs stay integral (min step exponent 0). Year and percentage cap max_step_exp at 0 so calendar years and percent-points never coarsen to a 10s/1000s quantum (1897 must not become 2000; 95 must not become 90). Snapping an already-snapped value at the same step is idempotent.

landmarks.$comment: Famous round-number giveaways that must be rejected when they sit adjacent to true_number. A candidate equal to a landmark within `proximity_permille` of |true| is a giveaway. Landmarks are exact integers/decimals with an explicit scale; the list is finite and unique. The grid is 0 plus the human-salient round numbers {1, 2, 2.5, 5} x 10^k for k = 0..10 (2.5 stored as 25 x 10^-1), so quarter-marks like 25/250/2500 and decade powers like 2000/5000/10000 are gated just like the classic 10/100/1000.

zero_value_strategy.$comment: Additive candidate strategy when normalized true_number == 0. `year` immediately abstains with ZERO_OUTSIDE_YEAR_DOMAIN. Every other kind carries a finite, strictly increasing, NONZERO ordered offset sequence per canonical surprise (index 0..3). Offsets are tried on the trap-preferred side in list order, then (when opposite-side fallback is permitted) on the opposite side; forced-side re-derivation never crosses sides. Offsets are exact integers/decimals with an explicit scale. All offsets are nonzero and finite by construction; the generator rejects any zero or non-finite offset.

display.$comment: Display/formatting rules used by the displayed-value collision gate and canonical output. Numbers >= grouping_threshold use thousands grouping. `decimal_places_by_kind` fixes how many decimals a kind renders so a candidate and truth that render identically after formatting are rejected as a display collision (Giveaway Gate rule 3). All values are exact integers.

validation.$comment: Machine-checkable invariants the generator (scripts/gen_derivation_tables.mjs) enforces before emitting any runtime file. These are declarative assertions over the sections above; the generator fails closed if any is violated.

monotonic_surprise_bands.description: For base_distance_bands and every kind_band_conversions interval list, both min and max are non-decreasing across adjacent canonical surprise values 0->1->2->3.

completeness.description: Every quantity_kind in closed_sets.quantity_kind has an entry in kind_strategies, bounds_defaults, hard_boundaries, dead_zones.kinds, snapping.kind_steps, and display.decimal_places_by_kind; canonical_surprise covers keys 0-3 and legacy keys 4-10; every non-year kind has zero_value_strategy offsets for surprise 0-3.

uniqueness.description: closed_sets have no duplicate members; landmarks.values are unique by (value, scale); candidate_order.slot_walk is a permutation of 0..slot_count-1; remedy_stages indices are unique and contiguous from 0.

finite_sequences.description: candidate_order.remedy_stages, snapping.refinement_sequence, and every zero_value_strategy offset list are finite and non-empty; slot_count and proximity/window values are finite non-negative integers.

nonzero_zero_strategy_offsets.description: Every offset in zero_value_strategy.offsets is a finite, nonzero, strictly increasing integer within its declared scale; no zero or non-finite offset is permitted.

fixed_point_only.description: All shared numbers are exact integer/fixed-point encodings (permille factors, integer/decimal mantissas with explicit scale). No binary floating literal is stored; the generator rejects any non-integer numeric literal outside declared decimal-scale contexts.
